Task (from the session that started this one):
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer, with a v2 cloud server at jusprinv2.obico.io. Kenneth wants promotions on the app's Account page that the server controls, so he can change or end them without an app release.

The frame runs no scripts because of a security check made during design. On macOS (tested) and Linux (from the wxWidgets source), wxWidgets puts the app's native bridge, `window.wx`, into every frame of a web view, not only the main page. When a message arrives, it doesn't tell the app which frame sent it. A test with a bare WKWebView, set up the way wxWidgets sets one up, showed that a sandboxed frame from another site that allows scripts can post to the native handler. With `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` and no `allow-scripts`, the frame's script didn't run, and the parent page could still read the frame's height. So the box must never get `allow-scripts`.

Old app versions rely only on two things: the endpoint exists, and it returns HTML or nothing. The box's content can change freely.

Task:
Build the server-filled box near the top of Preferences › Account in JusPrin, plus the server request that fills it. Its first use is a launch-promotion banner.

What it does (Kenneth agreed to this design on 2026-11-06):
- When Account opens, the app sends a small request, `GET /v2/account_box`, to the JusPrin v2 server. It sends the sign-in token when there is one, and no token when signed out.
- The server answers with a piece of HTML, or with nothing. Nothing means no box at all: no gap and no placeholder.
- The app puts the HTML in an `<iframe sandbox="allow-same-origin" srcdoc=…>`. That frame runs no scripts, so nothing inside it can reach the app's native bridge, and links in it can't open. The box is words and pictures only.
- The Account page measures the frame's content height itself and shows the box only after it has loaded and been sized. While it loads, nothing shows.
- The box also stays hidden when the request fails, when the app is offline, and when the app runs on the person's own API key. A failed request must not break or delay the rest of Account.
- The server decides what to send for each person:
  - signed out: "Sign up today" plus the offer;
  - signed in but never paid: the offer;
  - subscribed, or has ever bought a credit pack: nothing.
- The launch offer's wording: label "LAUNCH CELEBRATION", headline "Double credits on everything", body "Until 31 Jan, every credit pack and every month of every plan gives twice the credits." For a signed-out person the body starts with "Sign up today. ".
- The look is a brand gradient (orbit → violet → bloom) with small sparkles. The server's HTML carries its own styles, because the app's CSS doesn't reach inside the frame.

Where things are:
- Design board: "Plan and billing · Preferences › Account" on the JusPrin v2 canvas, https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ (Credits & plans page, from y=2900). Read it with the Artifact tool's read action.
- Spec, untracked: `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/money-pages-app-server-split-2026-11-06.md`. Item 5 of the contract, and the bridge finding under "Constraints found".
- App: Preferences is a web page in an `AgentWebView` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Preferences/PreferencesWindow.cpp`). Find its Account section in the web UI sources, and find how the page reads the account answer today (`/v2/account`).
- Server: the repo that holds `web_ent/jusprin/ledger/account.py`, which builds the existing `/v2/account` answer. Add the new endpoint beside it. Decide "has ever paid" from the ledger's records of subscriptions and purchased credits. The promotion end date belongs in one server-side setting, so the box disappears after 31 Jan without a deploy.

Done looks like:
- Server: the endpoint returns the right answer for each of the three cases, with tests.
- App: on a local build pointed at a local server, the box shows for a signed-out person and for a never-paid person, and doesn't show for a paying person or when the server is down. Take screenshots of each.
- A test proves a `<script>` inside the box never runs. Write that test so it fails if the sandbox attribute is loosened.
- Follow the repo's `AGENTS.md`: design tokens only in app code, the shared-machine build rules (`-j4`, check `pgrep -fl ninja` first), and `agent-docs/jusprin/design-guidelines.md` for on-screen text.
- Ask Kenneth before committing, and say how you propose to land it.

Out of scope:
- The in-app sheet for the server's full pricing and billing pages. That sheet also needs a web view without the native bridge, which is separate work.
- Any links or buttons inside the box.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_e71c8b0a-6720-4250-85de-80d4899e6200

# Money pages: which parts the app draws, which the server draws (2026-11-06)

Boards: canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ, page "Credits & plans", from y=2900 (version 131). Builder: figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_money_page.py.

## Agreed by Kenneth on 2026-11-06

- The server's pages open in a sheet inside the app, not in the browser.
- The one-time purchase is called "Credit pack".
- The launch offer doubles every credit amount until the end of January: a pack gives 1,000 instead of 500, Hobby 1,500 a month instead of 750, Workshop 2,000 instead of 1,000. It should look celebratory: the boards show a gradient banner, "Double credits on everything", and a "2× launch bonus" badge with the usual amount struck through on every card.
- Account shows the plan's price as a line the server sends; no price is hardcoded in the app.
- Delete account lives at the end of Preferences › Account, not on the server's page.
- Usage per day and per chat lives on the server's page, now "Billing and usage", not in the app.
- The app sends each chat's title to the server with its usage, and the server keeps it beside the chat id.
- Near the top of Preferences › Account sits a box the server fills: words and pictures in a frame, hidden when the server sends nothing. It has no links or buttons. The server decides per person: signed out, "sign up today"; signed in but never paid, the offer; subscribed or bought a pack, nothing. First use: the launch offer during the promotion.
- The "tell me when a plan would cost less" choice sits on the Credit pack card of the pricing page, not in Preferences. Auto-reload is offered there and on Billing and usage.

Everything below that is not in this list is a proposal.

## The rule (proposal)

The app draws credits. The server draws anything about money, inside a sheet the app owns. Where the app shows a price, it shows a sentence the server wrote and never works out a price itself.

## Who draws what (proposal)

App (ships with each release):
- **The sheet:** its frame, title, "Open in browser", close button, loading state and can't-load state. Never the page inside it.
- **Welcome and Home's agent card:** the 500-credit offer and a "See prices" link.
- **Composer:** ring and balance panel, credit prices on the model picker, "About 25 credits left", the out-of-credits card, "+1,000 credits" after buying.
- **Preferences › Account:** plan name with the server-sent price line, a bar per kind of credit, and Delete account (the app's own confirmation dialog, whose sentence the server sends; then DELETE /v2/account and sign out). "Get more credits", the ring's "See usage" and "Billing and usage" open the sheet.
- **Print history:** the report button and "25 credits added".

Server (jusprinv2.obico.io), shown in the sheet:
- **Credits and plans**, signed in or signed out.
- **On the Credit pack card:** auto-reload (off until ticked; buys a pack when the balance drops below 10 credits, Kenneth's pick) and the plan-savings alert (on by default).
- **Chargebee checkout**, as today.
- **Purchase done:** says what was added and to which account. Its "Back to your chat" button goes to the done address.
- **Billing and usage:** plan in dollars, Change plan, Cancel plan, Chargebee's portal for payment method and invoices, credits left, and credits used per day and per chat. The server doesn't know chat titles today (`account.py` names a row by its chat id). The app sends each chat's current title with its requests and the server stores it beside the chat id; the newest title wins, so renames show. Rows from app versions that send no title need a fallback name.
- **Server-written lines:** the plan's price line, the delete warning and the savings alert.

## The contract (the only part old app versions depend on; proposal)

1. **GET /v2/account, as today.** The server only adds fields; the app ignores fields it doesn't know. New fields: the plan's price line and the delete warning, each a finished sentence; the price line reads a finished sentence such as "$16 a month with Obico Premium's 20% off".
2. **POST /v2/web_link {page: "prices" | "billing", from}** returns a URL that signs in once as the app's account. The sheet opens it, and "Open in browser" asks for a fresh one. The server answers those page names forever; a name it doesn't know opens Credits and plans. Today the app builds the pricing URL itself (`AgentConfiguration.cpp`, `cloud_pricing_url`), so this replaces that.
3. **The done address, /v2/web/done.** When the sheet reaches it, the app closes the sheet and reads the account answer again. Checkout, a plan change and a cancel all end there. Closing with × also re-reads the account answer.
4. **DELETE /v2/account** deletes the account; the app then signs out.
5. **The server box on Account.** A small request, GET /v2/account_box, sent with the sign-in token when there is one, so it also answers signed-out people. It returns the box's HTML or nothing; nothing means no box. The Account page puts the HTML in a frame sandboxed with scripts off (`sandbox="allow-same-origin"`, via `srcdoc`), measures its height itself, and only then shows it. With scripts off, nothing in the box can reach the app, and links can't open, so the box is words and pictures only. The HTML brings its own styles; it can't use the app's CSS. Old app versions depend only on "HTML or nothing".
6. **The `suggestion` slot** in the account answer (`web_ent/jusprin/ledger/account.py`, unused today) carries the savings alert as {text, page}. The app shows the text as written.

## Constraints found

- **Google sign-in can't run inside a web view.** Google blocks OAuth in embedded web views on purpose. So the signed-out sheet's buttons read "Sign up to buy": they close the sheet and put the person on the app's own sign-up card. Source: https://developers.googleblog.com/2021/06/upcoming-security-changes-to-googles-oauth-2.0-authorization-endpoint.html
- **Chargebee supports its hosted checkout inside an app's web view.** It ships a React Native wrapper for exactly that. Its rule that digital goods must use in-app purchases applies to iOS and Android apps, not to a desktop app downloaded from our own site. Source: https://chargebee.com/checkout-portal-docs/react-native-wrapper-for-mobile.html
- **Unverified:** whether a card's bank check (3-D Secure) completes inside the sheet. Test with Chargebee's test cards before building.
- **Unverified:** browser-saved cards and password-manager extensions probably don't fill in inside the sheet. "Open in browser" covers that.

- **The app's native bridge reaches frames inside its pages (macOS: tested; Linux: from source).** wxWidgets adds `window.wx` to every frame, not just the page (`webview_webkit.mm`, `forMainFrameOnly:NO`; GTK uses `INJECT_ALL_FRAMES`), and hands the app the message without saying which frame sent it. A test with a plain WKWebView set up the same way: a sandboxed frame from another origin called `window.wx.postMessage` and the native handler received it. A frame with scripts allowed could therefore send the Account page's bridge messages, such as sign out. The box above avoids this by running no scripts: tested the same way, with `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` the frame's script didn't run, nothing reached the native side, and the parent page read the frame's height. Should a frame ever need scripts, the fix (proposal, JusPrin code only) is a per-load secret the app hands the main page by running a script, which runs in the main frame only; the app drops bridge messages without it. Windows (WebView2) is unchecked; its iframe messages probably arrive on a different event that wx doesn't listen to.
- **The sheet must not carry the bridge either.** `WebView::CreateWebView` adds the bridge to every web view it makes, so the sheet that shows the server's pages needs a web view created without it.

## Open

- The launch offer's edge case is my reading, not Kenneth's words: a subscription month billed on or before 31 Jan gets double.
- The proration line on Change plan is a placeholder for Chargebee's setting.
- Boards 5a and 5b (the old pricing page) and 4b's "Pay as you go" are superseded. A note on the canvas says so; their builder is unchanged.

"""What GET /ent/jusprin/v2/account answers: numbers and names only, so the app
can keep reading it for years."""
from datetime import timedelta
from typing import Dict, Optional

from django.conf import settings
from django.db.models import Count, Sum
from django.db.models.functions import TruncDate
from django.utils import timezone

from app_ent.models import Subscription
from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan
from .ledger import active_v2_plan, ensure_lots, live_lots
from .models import CreditCharge, CreditGrant
from .reports import report_activity

USAGE_DAYS = 30


def _lot(grant: CreditGrant) -> Dict:
    return {
        'kind': grant.kind,
        'credits': grant.credits_remaining,
        'granted': grant.credits_granted,
        'expires_at': grant.expires_at.isoformat() if grant.expires_at else None,
    }


def _plan(user) -> Optional[Dict]:
    plan = active_v2_plan(user.id)
    if plan is None:
        return None
    spec = settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS[plan.plan_id]
    subscription = Subscription.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    return {
        'id': plan.plan_id,
        'name': spec['name'],
        'renews_at': plan.current_term_end.isoformat() if plan.current_term_end else None,
        'unlimited_basic': bool(spec.get('unlimited_basic')),
        'obico_discount': bool(subscription and subscription.active()),
        'auto_reload': False,
    }


def _v1_subscription(user) -> Optional[Dict]:
    """The v1 subscription a person keeps the price of, for the welcome-back
    window. Read only: moving them to Hobby is billing's work."""
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user=user).first()
    if plan is None or not plan.is_active or plan.plan_id not in settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS:
        return None
    return {'plan_id': plan.plan_id, **settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS[plan.plan_id]}


def _usage(user, now) -> Dict:
    charges = CreditCharge.objects.filter(user=user, created_at__gte=now - timedelta(days=USAGE_DAYS))
    by_tier = {row['tier']: row for row in charges.values('tier').annotate(turns=Count('id'), credits=Sum('credits'))}
    dated = charges.annotate(date=TruncDate('created_at'))
    days = dated.values('date').annotate(credits=Sum('credits')).order_by('date')
    # The gateway never sees a chat's title, so a row names the chat by its id.
    rows = dated.values('date', 'chat_id', 'tier').annotate(messages=Count('id'), credits=Sum('credits'))
    activity = [{'date': row['date'].isoformat(), 'chat_id': row['chat_id'], 'tier': row['tier'],
                 'messages': row['messages'], 'credits': row['credits']} for row in rows]
    activity += report_activity(user, now - timedelta(days=USAGE_DAYS))
    activity.sort(key=lambda row: row['date'], reverse=True)
    return {
        'basic_turns': by_tier.get(CreditCharge.BASIC, {}).get('turns', 0),
        'expert_turns': by_tier.get(CreditCharge.EXPERT, {}).get('turns', 0),
        'credits': sum(row['credits'] for row in by_tier.values()),
        'days': [{'date': row['date'].isoformat(), 'credits': row['credits']} for row in days],
        'activity': activity,
    }


def account(user) -> Dict:
    now = timezone.now()
    ensure_lots(user.id, now)
    # A spent lot that still has an expiry keeps its bar ("0 of 500 left"); a
    # spent lot that never expires has nothing left to say.
    lots = [lot for lot in live_lots(user.id, now)
            if lot.credits_remaining > 0 or lot.expires_at is not None]
    return {
        'credits': {'total': sum(lot.credits_remaining for lot in lots), 'lots': [_lot(lot) for lot in lots]},
        'plan': _plan(user),
        'v1_subscription': _v1_subscription(user),
        'prices': {
            'credit_cents': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_CREDIT_CENTS,
            'pack': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK,
            'plans': [{'id': plan_id, **spec} for plan_id, spec in settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS.items()],
        },
        'usage_30d': _usage(user, now),
        'suggestion': None,
    }

---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

import json

from django.conf import settings
from django.http import HttpResponse, JsonResponse
from django.shortcuts import render
from django.utils import timezone
from django.views.decorators.csrf import csrf_exempt
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET, require_POST
from lib.file_storage import save_file_obj
from PIL import Image, UnidentifiedImageError

from jusprin.ledger.account import account as account_summary
from jusprin.ledger.ledger import ensure_lots
from jusprin.ledger.models import PrintReport
from jusprin.ledger.reports import ReportRefused, is_reported, submit_report

from .aliases import get_aliases
from .auth import authenticate
from .errors import error_body


@require_GET
def models(request):
    """The aliases this person can pick, in display order. "format" is the
    backend the person is currently assigned for the alias, and so the
    endpoint the client should use for a new chat."""
    user = authenticate(request)
    if user is None:
        return HttpResponse(error_body('unauthorized'), status=401, content_type='application/json')
    ensure_lots(user.id)
    data = [{
        'id': alias.id,
        'label': alias.label,
        'format': alias.group_for(user.id).format,
        'efforts': list(alias.efforts),
        # Left out when there is none: released apps read it as a string.
        **({'default_effort': alias.default_effort} if alias.default_effort else {}),
        'tier': alias.tier,
        'credits': alias.credits,
        'images': alias.backends[alias.group_for(user.id).format].images,
    } for alias in get_aliases().values()]
    response = JsonResponse({'data': data})
    response['Cache-Control'] = 'no-store'
    return response


@require_GET
def account(request):
    """The person's credits, plan and usage, for the composer's balance ring and
    the pre-send check."""
    user = authenticate(request)
    if user is None:
        return HttpResponse(error_body('unauthorized'), status=401, content_type='application/json')
    response = JsonResponse(account_summary(user))
    response['Cache-Control'] = 'no-store'
    return response


# Where the desktop app's loopback server sends the browser after it finishes,
# or fails, the OAuth code exchange.
@require_GET
def signed_in(request):
    return render(request, 'jusprin/v2/sign_in_result.html', {
        'heading': "You're signed in to JusPrin",
        'line': 'You can close this tab and go back to JusPrin.',
    })


@require_GET
def sign_in_failed(request):
    return render(request, 'jusprin/v2/sign_in_result.html', {
        'heading': "Signing in didn't finish",
        'line': 'Go back to JusPrin and try again.',
    })


def _refuse(code: str, status: int) -> HttpResponse:
    return HttpResponse(error_body(code), status=status, content_type='application/json')


def _decodable(photo) -> bool:
    try:
        with Image.open(photo) as image:
            image.verify()
        return True
    except (UnidentifiedImageError, OSError, SyntaxError, Image.DecompressionBombError):
        return False
    finally:
        photo.seek(0)


def _store_photos(user, gcode_hash: str, photos) -> list:
    stamp = str(timezone.now().timestamp())
    urls = []
    for index, photo in enumerate(photos):
        path = f'print_reports/{user.id}/{gcode_hash}/{stamp}_{index}'
        _, url = save_file_obj(path, photo, settings.TIMELAPSE_CONTAINER, user.syndicate.name, long_term_storage=True)
        urls.append(url)
    return urls


@csrf_exempt
@require_POST
def print_reports(request):
    """A person's report on how a print came out. Multipart: gcode_hash, outcome,
    text, facts (a JSON object) and one or more photos."""
    user = authenticate(request)
    if user is None:
        return _refuse('unauthorized', 401)
    gcode_hash = request.POST.get('gcode_hash', '').strip()
    outcome = request.POST.get('outcome', '')
    text = request.POST.get('text', '').strip()
    try:
        facts = json.loads(request.POST.get('facts', '{}'))
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return _refuse('invalid_request', 400)
    if not gcode_hash or outcome not in dict(PrintReport.OUTCOMES) or not isinstance(facts, dict):
        return _refuse('invalid_request', 400)
    if len(text) < settings.JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_MIN_TEXT:
        return _refuse('text_too_short', 400)
    photos = request.FILES.getlist('photos')
    if not photos:
        return _refuse('photo_needed', 400)
    if len(photos) > settings.JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_MAX_PHOTOS or any(photo.size > settings.JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_MAX_PHOTO_BYTES for photo in photos):
        return _refuse('request_too_large', 413)
    if not all(_decodable(photo) for photo in photos):
        return _refuse('photo_unreadable', 400)
    # Checked before the photos are stored; the unique constraint settles a race.
    if is_reported(user, gcode_hash):
        return _refuse('already_reported', 409)
    try:
        report = submit_report(user, gcode_hash, outcome, text, facts, _store_photos(user, gcode_hash, photos))
    except ReportRefused as refused:
        return _refuse(refused.code, 409)
    return JsonResponse({'id': report.id, 'credits': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_REPORT_CREDITS,
                         'created_at': report.created_at.isoformat()}, status=201)

def authenticate(request):
    """The active user whose OAuth2 bearer token the request carries, or None.

    The same check DRF's OAuth2Authentication runs for the v1 JusPrin views: any
    valid token of the provider, whichever application issued it, no scope
    required. A deactivated account's token is refused as well.
    """
    valid, oauthlib_request = get_oauthlib_core().verify_request(request, scopes=[])
    if not valid or not oauthlib_request.user.is_active:

    return oauthlib_request.user

"""The credit ledger: lots of credits and what each charged turn took from them.

Balance is the sum of the lots still live, never a stored number, and a lot's
expiry is a comparison at read and charge time, so a lot simply stops counting.
"""
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import models


class CreditGrant(models.Model):
    """One lot of credits."""
    PACK = 'pack'
    SUBSCRIPTION = 'subscription'
    SIGNUP = 'signup'
    FREE = 'free'
    REWARD = 'reward'
    LAUNCH_BONUS = 'launch_bonus'
    KINDS = [(k, k) for k in (PACK, SUBSCRIPTION, SIGNUP, FREE, REWARD, LAUNCH_BONUS)]

    user = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    kind = models.CharField(max_length=16, choices=KINDS)
    credits_granted = models.IntegerField()
    credits_remaining = models.IntegerField()
    expires_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)  # null: never
    # What makes the lot one of a kind for this person: signup, free:<n>,
    # report:<print report id>, and the invoice and subscription refs of billing.
    source_ref = models.CharField(max_length=128)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        constraints = [models.UniqueConstraint(fields=['user', 'source_ref'], name='jusprin_credit_grant_once')]
        indexes = [models.Index(fields=['user', 'expires_at'])]

    def __str__(self):
        return f'{self.user_id} {self.source_ref}: {self.credits_remaining}/{self.credits_granted}'


class CreditCharge(models.Model):
    """One per charged turn. credits is 0 for a basic turn on a plan that includes
    them, and for a turn the app started."""
    BASIC = 'basic'
    EXPERT = 'expert'
    TIERS = [(BASIC, BASIC), (EXPERT, EXPERT)]
    PERSON = 'person'
    APP = 'app'
    ORIGINS = [(PERSON, PERSON), (APP, APP)]

    user = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    turn_id = models.CharField(max_length=128)
    chat_id = models.CharField(max_length=32, null=True, blank=True)
    alias = models.CharField(max_length=64)
    tier = models.CharField(max_length=8, choices=TIERS)
    credits = models.IntegerField()
    origin = models.CharField(max_length=8, choices=ORIGINS)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        constraints = [models.UniqueConstraint(fields=['user', 'turn_id'], name='jusprin_credit_charge_once')]
        indexes = [models.Index(fields=['user', 'created_at'])]

    def __str__(self):
        return f'{self.user_id} {self.turn_id}: {self.credits}'


class CreditAllocation(models.Model):
    """Which lots paid a charge."""
    charge = models.ForeignKey(CreditCharge, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='allocations')
    grant = models.ForeignKey(CreditGrant, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='allocations')
    credits = models.IntegerField()


class PrintReport(models.Model):
    """What a person says about how a sliced print came out: the training-data
    channel, so it has its own table rather than a place in the gateway's chats."""
    WORKED = 'worked'
    PARTLY = 'partly'
    FAILED = 'failed'
    OUTCOMES = [(k, k) for k in (WORKED, PARTLY, FAILED)]

    user = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    gcode_hash = models.CharField(max_length=128)
    outcome = models.CharField(max_length=16, choices=OUTCOMES)
    text = models.TextField()
    # Sent by the app with the report: printer, material, process, slice
    # statistics, manufacturing input hash, and the project's name for the row.
    facts = models.JSONField(default=dict, blank=True)
    photos = models.JSONField(default=list)  # the stored photos' URLs
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        constraints = [models.UniqueConstraint(fields=['user', 'gcode_hash'], name='jusprin_print_report_once')]
        indexes = [models.Index(fields=['user', 'created_at'])]

    def __str__(self):
        return f'{self.user_id} {self.gcode_hash}: {self.outcome}'


class PrintReportReview(models.Model):
    """A person at Obico read the report."""
    report = models.OneToOneField(PrintReport, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    invalid = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    note = models.CharField(max_length=500, blank=True)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

"""Charging a turn against a person's lots of credits.

Every credit is the same. A turn costs its alias's price, except a turn the app
started by itself (the file-opened report, the slice-finished note) and a basic
message on an active Workshop plan, which cost nothing.
"""
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Dict, Optional

from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta
from django.conf import settings
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.db import transaction
from django.db.models import F, Q
from django.utils import timezone

from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan
from .models import CreditAllocation, CreditCharge, CreditGrant


class CreditsExhausted(Exception):
    """The next turn cannot be paid."""

    def __init__(self, balance: int, cost: int, plan: Optional[str]):
        super().__init__(f'{cost} credits needed, {balance} available')
        self.balance = balance
        self.cost = cost
        self.plan = plan

    def details(self) -> Dict:
        return {'balance': self.balance, 'cost': self.cost, 'plan': self.plan}


def _is_subscribed(user_id: int) -> bool:
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(user_id=user_id).first()
    return plan is not None and plan.is_active and (
        plan.plan_id in settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS or plan.plan_id in settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS)


def ensure_lots(user_id: int, now: datetime = None) -> None:
    """Creates the lots nobody buys: the first month's, once per account, and
    after it the free credits of an account without a subscription, a new lot
    once the last one has expired. Each lasts a month from the day it is granted.
    Lazy, in place of a monthly sweep over every account. Concurrent requests meet
    on the unique source_ref."""
    now = now or timezone.now()
    signup, _ = CreditGrant.objects.get_or_create(user_id=user_id, source_ref='signup', defaults={
        'kind': CreditGrant.SIGNUP,
        'credits_granted': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_SIGNUP_CREDITS,
        'credits_remaining': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_SIGNUP_CREDITS,
        'expires_at': now + relativedelta(months=1),
    })
    if now < signup.expires_at or _is_subscribed(user_id):
        return
    free = CreditGrant.objects.filter(user_id=user_id, kind=CreditGrant.FREE)
    if free.filter(expires_at__gt=now).exists():
        return
    CreditGrant.objects.get_or_create(user_id=user_id, source_ref=f'free:{free.count() + 1}', defaults={
        'kind': CreditGrant.FREE,
        'credits_granted': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_FREE_CREDITS,
        'credits_remaining': settings.JUSPRIN_V2_FREE_CREDITS,
        'expires_at': now + relativedelta(months=1),
    })


def live_lots(user_id: int, now: datetime):
    """The lots still counting, in draw order: the soonest to expire first,
    never-expiring last, oldest first within one expiry."""
    return (CreditGrant.objects
            .filter(Q(expires_at__isnull=True) | Q(expires_at__gt=now), user_id=user_id)
            .order_by(F('expires_at').asc(nulls_last=True), 'created_at', 'id'))


def lock_person(user_id: int) -> None:
    """Serialises everything that spends a person's lots, until the transaction
    ends. On the person's row because they may hold no live lot. no_key lets a new
    lot or charge pointing at that row go ahead."""
    get_user_model().objects.select_for_update(no_key=True).only('pk').get(pk=user_id)

"""GET /ent/jusprin/v2/account_box: the launch offer for people who have not
paid, nothing for those who have, and nothing once the offer ends."""
import uuid
from datetime import timedelta

from django.test import Client, TestCase, override_settings
from django.utils import timezone
from oauth2_provider.models import AccessToken, Application

from app.models import User
from jusprin.ledger.models import CreditGrant
from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan

URL = '/ent/jusprin/v2/account_box'
OFFER = 'Double credits on everything'
SIGN_UP = 'Sign up today. Until 31 Jan, every credit pack and every month of every plan gives twice the credits.'


class AccountBoxTests(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.user = User.objects.create(email=f'box-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com')
        app = Application.objects.create(
            client_id=f'JusPrin2-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}', name='JusPrin 2', client_type=Application.CLIENT_PUBLIC,
            authorization_grant_type=Application.GRANT_AUTHORIZATION_CODE, redirect_uris='http://127.0.0.1/callback')
        self.token = AccessToken.objects.create(user=self.user, application=app, token=uuid.uuid4().hex,
                                                scope='read write', expires=timezone.now() + timedelta(days=1)).token

    def signed_in(self):
        return Client().get(URL, HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f'Bearer {self.token}')

    def grant(self, kind, source_ref):
        CreditGrant.objects.create(user=self.user, kind=kind, credits_granted=500, credits_remaining=0,
                                   source_ref=source_ref, expires_at=timezone.now() - timedelta(days=40))

    def assertNoBox(self, response):
        self.assertEqual((response.status_code, response.content, response['Cache-Control']), (204, b'', 'no-store'))

    def test_signed_out_gets_sign_up_and_the_offer(self):
        response = Client().get(URL)
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual((response['Content-Type'], response['Cache-Control']), ('text/html; charset=utf-8', 'no-store'))
        self.assertContains(response, 'LAUNCH CELEBRATION')
        self.assertContains(response, OFFER)
        self.assertContains(response, SIGN_UP)

    def test_signed_in_never_paid_gets_the_offer_without_sign_up(self):
        response = self.signed_in()
        self.assertContains(response, OFFER)
        self.assertContains(response, 'Until 31 Jan, every credit pack')
        self.assertNotContains(response, 'Sign up')

    def test_free_and_report_credits_are_not_paying(self):
        self.grant(CreditGrant.FREE, 'free:1')
        self.grant(CreditGrant.REWARD, 'report:1')
        self.assertContains(self.signed_in(), OFFER)

    def test_anyone_who_ever_bought_a_pack_gets_nothing(self):
        self.grant(CreditGrant.PACK, 'inv:1')
        self.assertNoBox(self.signed_in())

    def test_anyone_who_ever_had_a_plan_gets_nothing_after_it_lapsed(self):
        self.grant(CreditGrant.SUBSCRIPTION, 'sub:1')
        JusPrinPlan.objects.create(user=self.user, plan_id='jusprin-hobby-monthly', external_id='x',
                                   external_user_id='y', expired_at=timezone.now() - timedelta(days=1))
        self.assertNoBox(self.signed_in())

    def test_a_subscriber_gets_nothing_before_the_plan_grants_credits(self):
        JusPrinPlan.objects.create(user=self.user, plan_id='jusprin-workshop-monthly', external_id='x',
                                   external_user_id='y')
        self.assertNoBox(self.signed_in())

    def test_a_v1_subscriber_gets_nothing(self):
        JusPrinPlan.objects.create(user=self.user, plan_id='jusprin-unlimited-annual', external_id='x',
                                   external_user_id='y')
        self.assertNoBox(self.signed_in())

    def test_a_token_that_no_longer_works_gets_nothing(self):
        AccessToken.objects.filter(token=self.token).update(expires=timezone.now() - timedelta(seconds=1))
        self.assertNoBox(self.signed_in())

    def test_nobody_gets_the_offer_once_it_ends(self):
        with override_settings(REDACTED.now()):
            self.assertNoBox(Client().get(URL))
            self.assertNoBox(self.signed_in())
        with override_settings(REDACTED.now() + timedelta(minutes=1)):
            self.assertContains(Client().get(URL), SIGN_UP)

    def test_the_box_has_no_script_and_no_link(self):
        # The app's frame runs no scripts and opens no links; neither would work.
        for response in (Client().get(URL), self.signed_in()):
            html = response.content.decode().lower()
            self.assertNotIn('<script', html)
            self.assertNotIn('<a ', html)

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

       ```tsx
       import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
       export function AccountBox({ html }: { html: string }) {
         const frame = useRef<HTMLIFrameElement>(null);
         const loaded = useRef(false);
         const [height, setHeight] = useState<number | null>(null);
         const measure = () => {
           const root = frame.current?.contentDocument?.documentElement;
           if (loaded.current && root) setHeight(Math.ceil(root.getBoundingClientRect().height));
         };
         useEffect(() => {
           const observer = new ResizeObserver(measure);
           observer.observe(frame.current!);
           return () => observer.disconnect();
           // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
         }, []);
         // onLoad, not a listener added after mounting: the content may load first.
         return (
           <iframe ref={frame} className="prefs-box" title="From JusPrin" sandbox="allow-same-origin" srcDoc={html}
             onLoad={() => { loaded.current = true; measure(); }}
             data-measuring={height === null ? '' : undefined} style={height === null ? undefined : { height }} />
         );
       }
       ```

## Bug found and fixed: a frame load disconnected the page

wx raises wxEVT_WEBVIEW_NAVIGATING for frames inside the page too (macOS `decidePolicyForNavigationAction`
fires for every frame). AgentWebView's handler reset the bridge handshake on every NAVIGATING, so the box's
`about:srcdoc` load disconnected Preferences: every later message from the page was refused with
"handshake_required", and 20 s later the window was replaced by "The Agent panel could not connect".
Seen in the real app (signed-out case) and in the shell harness before the fix.

Fix (AgentWebView.cpp, JusPrin-owned): NAVIGATING for an `about:` URL leaves the handshake alone. The URL
decides, not `event.GetInt()` (the main-frame flag), because wx's GTK backend never sets that flag.
EOF

name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata:

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

content.text:
The promotion box on Preferences › Account works end to end in the real app against a local server. It shows for signed-out and never-paid people. It stays hidden for paying people, when the server is down, and when the person uses their own API key. Nothing is committed yet in either repository.

**A bug the box exposed, now fixed.** wxWidgets sends its "page is navigating" event for frames inside a page, not only for the page itself. JusPrin reset the page's link to the app on every such event, so the box loading inside its frame cut that link. In the real app, every button on Preferences stopped working. Twenty seconds later the whole window was replaced by "The Agent panel could not connect". I saw this in the app before fixing it. The fix is in `AgentWebView.cpp`, a JusPrin-owned file: loads of `about:` URLs (which is what a frame filled with HTML from a string reports) no longer reset the link. I went by the URL rather than wx's main-frame flag because wx never sets that flag on Linux. After the fix, Preferences was still connected 40 seconds after the box loaded.

**What I tested:**
- **Server:** the 10 new tests pass, and so do all 170 JusPrin tests.
- **Page:** 692 tests pass. The sandbox test fails if the frame is allowed to run scripts.
- **App's message layer:** the native tests pass.
- **Box check in the test harness:** its 5 checks pass in the real WebKit view. With scripts allowed, 4 fail, because the box's script closes Preferences through `window.wx`. Before, that case made the harness hang until it timed out, so I changed its wait to end however the window closes.
- **Full default harness:** 600 checks pass, 0 failures.
- **Real app, all five cases:**
  - signed out: the box, with "Sign up today.";
  - signed in, never paid: the box, without "Sign up";
  - paying: no box and no gap;
  - server down: no box, and the rest of Account shows normally;

Only the Elegoo deployments need it; they turn it on in ML_API_ENT_SERVICES in their own manifests. TSD and local dev keep their current service lists.
---
Add an Elegoo API that detects a missing build plate from one photo

Elegoo's printer has ring markers printed on its magnetic pad. The build
plate covers them, so a marker visible in the chamber photo means the
plate is missing. New endpoint POST /ent/partners/api/elegoo/plate_presence/
takes the photo plus the unit's own measured marker positions and sizes
(`markers`), and an optional `tolerance` (default 50 px, max 100): how far
a detected marker center may be from the measured one. It answers
{"plate_missing": bool, "markers_found": [...]}, or 400 with an error for
any invalid measurement; nothing is guessed.

Django checks the device credentials, forwards only the photo and
measurements to a new ML API service (/plate_presence_p/, enabled with
`plate_presence` in ML_API_ENT_SERVICES), and stores each checked photo
with its measurements and answer in short-term storage, so false alarms
can be measured on field photos. The path keeps the printer id as its
second segment, which object storage shards on.

The service is classical CV, no model weights. The detector is ported
from the bullseye validation repo with its strict ring checks (contrast
>= 30 gray levels and >= 3x the pixel noise), which separate printed ink
from the textured build plate. The port matches bullseye.py exactly on
480 marker searches over real photos. With this setup on the DVT2 unit:
0 alarms in 2,500 plate-installed photos at three bed heights, and an
alarm in 116 of 117 bare-pad photos (110 of 117 when the measured
centers are off by up to 50 px). Nearly all detections come from the
front marker.

Not done here: the elegoo and elegoo-cn ML API deployments need
plate_presence in ML_API_ENT_SERVICES and an image rebuild.
